- When sentiment is negative and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If recent history shows strong upward momentum but forecast peaks too early, cap the peak at 1–2% above the 14-day moving average.  
- If sentiment is positive and forecast is falling, adjust downward by 3–5% to avoid premature reversal.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show mean reversion or consolidation, reduce forecast volatility by 15–20% to reflect reduced momentum.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, apply a 2–3% downward bias to all 30-day forecasts.  
- If forecast overshoots true outcome by >5% in 3 consecutive days, apply a 1–2% downward correction to next 3 days.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, use 14-day moving average as baseline, then adjust ±2% based on sentiment direction.
